label: an approximate reconstruction from the cited claims, not the experiment's geometry
subsystem: Time-of-Flight, four layers in two halves

quantities.name: half_x0
quantities.definition: x/X0 of the scintillator at normal incidence through one counter of each layer of a half, outside overlaps
quantities.derivation: 2 x 1 cm (ams02:C188) x 1.023 g/cm3 (ams02:C193) / 43.90 g/cm2 (PDG, polyvinyltoluene); NIM A 623 Table 3 states 4.7% (ams02:C196)

sources.source: PDG Atomic and Nuclear Properties, polyvinyltoluene (2024 web edition; 2025 identical)
sources.value: radiation length 43.90 g/cm2 (42.54 cm at 1.032 g/cm3)

independence.result: independent of Geant4: thickness and density from the TOF hardware papers and the manufacturer, radiation length PDG's tabulation; NIM A 623 does not say how Table 3 was computed. The reference is not a Geant4 output. Geant4 computes radiation lengths with the same Tsai formula, so agreement validates the geometry and the material definition (composition and density), not Geant4's radiation-length physics.

quantities.name: counters
quantities.definition: number of counters in the expanded IR

independence.result: a design count from the hardware paper, not a simulation output

approximations: the trapezoidal outer counters, whose outline no source dimensions, are rectangles of the largest width, 26 cm
every counter of a layer has the length of the layer's longest rectangular counter (NIM A 623 Table 2)
the upper and lower halves are 120 cm apart ('about 120 cm'), the two layers of a half adjacent
counters alternate by the 1.5 cm stagger in z; covers, supports and honeycomb (ams02:C196, C197) are not modelled
status: validated-in-scope (comparison with cited values, not confirmation)
